findings.title: Anonymous denial assertion does not independently prove AppCheck enforcement
findings.evidence: Request contains no authorization or AppCheck header and expects generic UNAUTHENTICATED. Same wrapper result is possible with enforceAppCheck false because Auth is absent.
findings.impact: SDK HTTP transport correction is useful, but AppCheck enforcement regression cannot be certified by this assertion alone.
findings.recommendation: Use discriminating valid owner Auth without AppCheck or verifier instrumentation proving AppCheck rejection; retain real browser token/missing-AppCheck acceptance gate.

boundedObservations: Deploy wrapper permits only backend/hosting single phase, fixed eleven names and fixed project; extra arguments rejected. Receipt ref/environment and current source candidate must bind; backend scope excludes finance/preferences/collector exports.

Hosting wrapper checks exact11 active function names, runtime identity and maxInstanceCount2 against candidate-matching readback. It does not itself certify readback timestamp/source authenticity, AppCheck, concurrency/memory, blockers or latest suite completion; lead must separately verify them.

Doctor verifies approval receipt path existence and candidate, deployment config metadata presence, blocker phase and non-emulator Firestore setting; declarative config booleans are not independent cloud readback.

addApp requires AppCheck via callable options, allowlisted verified Google token with revocation/project checks, active owner access, recent Auth and durable rate cap. Transaction rechecks owner access and revision, enforces idempotency and registry bound, records audit.

User-supplied sourceProjectId remains metadata with mappingVerified false; appDefinitions output passes only id/name to operations; RESOURCE_CATALOG compiled verified source list remains query authority.
Production addApp UI defaults disabled and requires explicit config flag; UI onboarding states source requires verification. Browser flag is feature availability, never authorization.

Sanity workflow uses content-read permission only, pinned actions, Node22 and dedicated demo emulators; no production deploy or secrets configured. Local green cannot establish live owner/AppCheck/provider readiness.
